why: The hour converged and did not go in circles. The closure was cut, the emptied modules removed, and it was re-run against the base commit until nothing new was orphaned. The two over-broad test-cut passes (string literals, then bare locals) were tightened and redone before anything was committed, which is a rule being narrowed, not an edit undone. There is no packing: this is deletion work, so no size, spacing or band is in play. The refusals were correct: shell-check caught a real backtick inside double quotes, and step-back-due is this checkpoint. The cost sat in the dead-closure tooling. About 20 of the 62 minutes went to ~600 s fixpoint runs (time.md lists them as `sed` and `cat`). The session had to find by hand what the census cannot see: a self-referencing island (citybudget.py's dataclasses and format_budget), class-level constants (_WARD_STROKE, _PADDY_ROCK_KINDS, the DOJO_* pair), and a second ring of 16 names orphaned only after modules were removed.
what: Go on to the first make done as planned. If it is red, read the coverage-floor and import phases first, because the AST test-cut passes are where live tests could have been lost.
tooling_fix: scripts/measure/dead_closure.py: add a --fixpoint mode that re-runs against --base until no new name is orphaned (dropping package re-exports of deleted names as it goes), and add class-level constants and groups of names reachable only from each other to its census, with a test for each, so the next deletion does not need hand-written exhibit_fix.py/finish392.py loops and hand checks.
